Wow, thanks for the detailed reply! It didn't occur to me that cognitive dissonance would prevent suspension of disbelief in that way.

I can understand regarding the China aspect. I pretty much picked it as a location because I'm familiar enough with it to write about it; it didn't occur to me that it'd be so predictable.

That said, I was attempting to get a feeling of isolation between Mark and Zyn, towards the end especially, to contrast with Sylvain's easygoing relations with the mages and other Serpent's Hand or Library associates he knows. If the Foundation interactions came off as Adorable Siblings!! then I'll need to work on that.

Again, thanks. Your feedback was quite enlightening.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I did. I liked that a bit better, though I didn't vote on it yet.

In terms of the self-insert thing: although I'm only newly active, I've been lurking for long enough to be passingly familiar with the character of Researcher Zyn Kiryu, and with the idea that she is, broadly speaking, 'you,' with Dr. Mark being who you would mainly use in a scip or etc. The pair of them together are actually among my favorite author avatars (matching turtlenecks!), so it's not that I don't like either or both of them!

But because, as a result of how the pair is set up, I strongly identify Researcher Zyn with the author Zyn, it's very hard to read things in which she is a prominent character, because you are a real biological researcher in real life whereas the Foundation is not a real organization. In terms of realism, it's not so much that Researcher Zyn is totally unbelievable per se; it's that the difficulty of removing her from her creator in my mind effectively blocks the suspension of disbelief by setting up cognitive dissonance between "these are fellow users of a wiki I read for fun" and "these are characters in a fictional universe I enjoy." For example, when I realized Researcher Zyn was going to go on a trip, I thought: "I bet this is going to be to China. Zyn recently went to China." Stuff like that makes it really hard to stay immersed, for me.

I haven't got time for (more of a!) detailed comment right now; I would, however, say that the interactions between Researcher Kiryu and Dr. Kiryu leaned a bit too much towards Adorable Siblings!! to be quite as believable as they needed to be given the type of workplace the Foundation is generally portrayed as being.

I hope that helps explain. :)

item.title: Author's Notes
item.content:encoded:
This is a duo tale, involving an associate of the Serpent’s Hand and a researcher of the Foundation, also known as the Jailers.

It’s best to read both sides of the tale, as they’re intended to fill in each other’s blanks. It’s up to the reader which perspective they are more inclined to favor.

Many thanks go to Silberescher, DrMann, and MisterFlames, and to Bunton and Pixeltasm. And naturally, to everyone else in the SCP and Wanderers’ Library chats who helped me bring months of thinking to words.
